key_insight: Barycentric distillation turns transductive Gromov-Wasserstein embeddings into an inductive neural mapping that preserves the teacher geometry for unseen samples.
engineering_relevance: This enables fast out-of-sample inference for multi-view representation learning without recomputing relational matrices or solving GW optimization at test time.
method: Train a GW-MDS teacher to learn a latent support and optimal transport coupling.
Use barycentric projection to convert the coupling into sample-aligned target embeddings.
Train a neural student with view-specific encoders, extending to Mean-GWMDS and Multi-GWMDS variants.
evidence_signal: The method was evaluated on synthetic and real-world datasets using Euclidean, geodesic, and cosine relations, and distilled models preserved teacher geometry while outperforming direct neural GW training on unseen samples.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality of the teacher coupling and barycentric targets, so noisy or unstable transport plans could affect student generalization.
paper_title: Gromov-Wasserstein Distillation for Inductive Multi-View Embedding
